market_holds: Spot 18.79 at the 18:09 UTC seal (sealed baseline); the stock closed at 14.04 on 2026-11-02 and has risen about 33% in eight sessions. Most of that came after AppLovin's Q3 (+55% y/y, Q4 guided +8-10% q/q) and Unity's Q3 (Vector +126% y/y, +40% q/q), on 11-04 and 11-05 (Yahoo bars; StockStory 2026-11-05). Front-expiry (11-20) event-implied move 24.7%, but the ATM spread is 63% of mid and put/call OI is 0.4, so it is call-heavy and the number is only indicative (baseline). The only prior print (Q2, 2026-08-12, amc) beat revenue consensus by about 6% ($220M against about $208M), guided Q3 flat sequentially at $217-222M, and fell 5.6% at the next open and 20.6% by the close (Yahoo bars). Q3 revenue consensus is about $221M (Benzinga $221.3M, Earnings Whispers $220.9M), in the top half of the guide; EPS consensus $0.17 with a $0.20 whisper (finviz/EW 2026-11-04). The FY26 guide is $870-880M revenue and $510-518M adj. EBITDA, which implies about $229.5M for Q4 at the Q3 midpoint. The sell side is mostly Buy with a $33-35 average target; Piper initiated at Neutral/$19 on 09-22, citing AppLovin and Unity competition. The lock-up expires 11-30. Blackstone holds 49.5% (83.8M of about 169M shares, 13G/A 2026-11-06), and the IPO float was only 21.9M shares at $23, so the stock trades below its IPO price.
view: The quarter itself probably beats. The guide was explicitly 'prudent', it excludes unconfirmed model gains, and it was set flat sequentially after a World Cup-boosted Q2, against a 2025 pattern of about +10% from Q2 to Q3 (implied by the 21-24% y/y Q3 guide). Every peer that has reported the September quarter was strong: AppLovin +55%, Unity Vector +40% q/q, Digital Turbine's AGP +42% with a raised FY guide. Prediction-market ad spend was up sharply through July. Any Q3 beat forces a FY raise, or Q4 would be implied down sequentially, so 'beat and raise' is the likely headline. Management's executive option awards vest on the VWAP in the three months after the lock-up, which gives them a reason to guide confidently this time rather than sandbag. Against that, the market has already moved: the stock is up 33% from its 11-02 low on exactly that peer read-through and sits back at its post-Q2 trading level. The whisper is above consensus. The one prior print showed this stock trades on the forward guide and the growth trajectory, not on the beat. Two things can still disappoint at the open: the Q4 guide and margins (Q3 EBITDA margin was guided down to 57-58% from 60%). Unity's Vector taking share in gaming user acquisition is a live risk to the half of revenue that is gaming. The float is thin, so an after-hours print swings far either way. Net: a modest lean up and no edge I would bet on.
unpriced: Possibly the size of the forced FY raise. Consensus sits only at the top of a guide that peers' September-quarter growth makes look conservative. But the 33% eight-session run-up after the peer prints is direct price evidence that the read-through is largely held, so I cannot show a gap.

recommendation.reason: A beat and a forced FY raise look likely given conservative guidance and strong peer prints. But the stock has already rallied about 33% in eight sessions on that same peer read-through, and its only prior print sold off on the forward guide despite a 6% beat. I cannot show the price lacks the beat, so the direction is not above 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 guide clearly above the roughly $229.5M implied by the current FY range (for example $240M or more, or FY $895M or more) with steady 59-60% margins would make an up open likely. A Q4 guide at or below the implied number, or commentary on gaming share loss to Unity or AppLovin, would make a down open likely.

self_critique: The case for long is the textbook new-IPO pattern: conservative guide, strong peers, a forced raise, management incentives tied to post-lock-up prices, and a stock 19% below its $23 IPO price at about 8x EV/EBITDA. If the raise is large, a thin float could gap 15%+ up. The case for short: the 33% run-up in eight sessions plus a whisper above consensus means a merely in-line raise disappoints. The only prior print sold off on the guide despite a 6% beat. The 11-30 lock-up of about 147M shares gives holders a reason to sell any strength. Neither case moves me past the high 50s.
approach_notes: P4 (priced-in is a claim to prove) helped: the run-up after the peer prints was direct price evidence that the read-through is held. P6's 'find the line it trades on' was answered by the one prior print. The baseline's to-expiry implied move overstates an open-scored window, and the playbook says nothing about adjusting for that.
